content: Pavement Management Systems (PMS) -- the mature domain analog to RoadTwin -- use a three-stage architecture: sensor/inspection-derived measurement -> calibration -> index aggregation into homogeneous road sections, producing a Pavement Condition Index (0-100 scale, deduct-value method) per segment. Condition data aggregation into segments is a distinct algorithmic step from raw distress detection, using a 'lowest common denominator' / minimum-segment-length approach; GIS dynamic segmentation tools (ArcGIS, and by extension PostGIS) partition the network and reconcile segment boundaries over time. This confirms segment-first aggregation (not report-first) and a distinct index/scoring stage after aggregation is the domain-standard architecture, matching RoadTwin's RoadSegment -> RoadHealth split.
